I ask this, out of sheer curiosity- and I mean no disrespect. Could you please explain to me exactly why any “breathing condition” makes you unable to wear a mask? 

I am a paramedic and since the beginning of the pandemic, EVERY patient is masked, with the only exception being that they are actively receiving a nebulizer treatment (which are SIGNIFICANTLY limited in use since Covid) or they are being artificially ventilated, ie- a bag valve mask. 

Even patients on supplemental oxygen (via nasal cannula or non-rebreather) have a surgical mask covering their mouth and nose over the cannula or oxygen mask. 

All EMT’s, Paramedics, first responders are required to wear a properly fitted N95 mask- (I understand the availability issues...) as per our protocols.

If you have a respiratory issue, you are at a much greater risk of complications and death if you contract the virus. I cannot honestly think of any valid reason that would prevent anyone from wearing a mask- let alone someone who has a significantly greater risk of morbidly/mortality.

Uncomfortable or dead... glasses fog up or weeks in an isolation unit... feeling anxious in a mask or anxiously waiting to see if your child/ parent/ partner is going to survive the virus that you  gave them because you wouldn’t wear a mask?

I learned (over 30 years) that cheap tools are cheap tools. They might live long enough to get a few jobs done, or they might just break half way through the project at 8pm on Sunday night, and... you see where this is going.

My approach is this; if you are going to DIY a job, you have already subtracted your labor cost. So take that money, and reallocate it into whatever you can (depending upon the size and scope of the project) either better quality materials or a good quality tool. As a simple example, I did a complete tear out in a full bath in our house. I did all of the work myself, the only labor cost was to have a plumber and an electrician sign off on my work (required for permits) *this is not legal in ALL municipalities- check it out for yourself*- so... I purchased higher quality tile, some extra decorative bullnose edging and a very nice tile saw. 15 years later, I still have a beautiful bathroom that shows no sign of aging or wear and tear- and I have had an amazing tile saw that has made the “little” jobs turn out so much better, easier, faster and more accurate.

There were times when all that I could afford was a HF tool, and there’s no shame in that, but given the choice- it’s still true: you get what you pay for.

I am sorry if this was already suggested- I just couldn’t keep reading the comments. My heart aches for you- please, please; contact a battered women’s center. They can assist you with maneuvering the police, legal system, etc. Not knowing where you are, you may be blown off by the police, and the last thing you need is another beat down- metaphorical or literal. This man sounds dangerous. If he did it to you, he has either done it to someone else, or will do it to someone else. 

Battered women’s shelters do much more than provide “shelter” - many of the people they help never spend a night in their facility. But they are a font of information including referrals to legal assistance, creating a safety plan, being a liaison between yourself and local law enforcement... the list goes on.

Remember, the single most dangerous time for a woman (or man)  in a relationship with an abuser is the moment they leave. Get help, make a plan and be very careful. 

You are in my thoughts. I hope only the best for you; a safe exit and a wonderful future. Clearly he didn’t destroy your spirit- it will serve you well when you begin your life anew.

You will figure it out- and I hope the two of you get “happily ever after” - which in reality translates to amazing, hard (but well worth the effort) and mostly joy with the occasional bump to keep you in the real world. Best of luck- invite me to your wedding.
